title: How many switches does two-Hamiltonian universality require?
abstract: Any pair of sufficiently generic Hamiltonians on $\mathbb{C}^d$ generates the full unitary group, i.e., any $W\in U(d)$ can be synthesized to arbitrary precision by alternating between the two evolutions for suitably chosen durations. For any given pair of Hamiltonians, the minimal number of switches required to cover the entire group is at least $d$ and unbounded in general. Despite this, we show that it scales linearly in $d$ in expectation. Assuming that the two spectra are sufficiently generic, we derive constructive upper bounds on the minimal switching number as a function of the change-of-basis matrix between the two eigenbases. In particular, if this matrix has a column whose entries all have equal moduli, as for a complex Hadamard matrix, then $9d$ switches suffice to reach every unitary. To obtain these results, we construct a short exact representation of any unitary as a product of unitaries that are alternately diagonal in two given bases. All bounds are extended to non-generic spectra and bounded evolution times.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes the problem of quantum control, specifically determining the minimum number of alternating Hamiltonian evolutions needed to approximate any desired unitary transformation in a $d$-dimensional system. It establishes that this number scales linearly with dimension for generic systems and provides explicit, quantifiable upper bounds for the required switches and evolution times.
main_problem: The paper determines the minimal number of switches required to synthesize an arbitrary unitary evolution $W \in U(d)$ by alternating between two fixed Hamiltonian evolutions, $e^{it_1 H_1} e^{it_2 H_2} \cdots$.
main_result: For generic spectra, the required number of switches scales linearly with the dimension $d$, and explicit upper bounds are derived based on the structure of the change-of-basis matrix.
method: The analysis uses group theory and Lie theory concepts, relating the Hamiltonian universality problem to the representation of unitaries as products of diagonal unitaries in two different bases.
model_or_system: The model is quantum control on a $d$-dimensional Hilbert space ($\mathbb{C}^d$), where the dynamics are governed by two Hamiltonians, $H_1$ and $H_2$. The goal is to approximate the full unitary group $U(d)$ using alternating time evolution steps.
key_observables: The minimal number of switches ($\ell$ or $n$), the approximation error ($\|W - V\|$ in operator norm), and the required evolution times ($T, T'$).
important_parameters: System dimension ($d$), the structure of the Hamiltonians ($H_1, H_2$), and the spectral properties (linear independence over $\mathbb{Q}$) of their eigenvalues.
main_assumptions: The initial results assume 'sufficiently generic' spectra; later theorems provide rigorous bounds by assuming positive spectral gaps ($\delta_M > 0$) to achieve arbitrary accuracy.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the general problem of Hamiltonian universality to deriving structural bounds ($	ext{LQ}(U)$) based on spectral properties, and finally providing explicit, quantifiable upper bounds on the number of switches and required time scales for achieving high-accuracy approximation of any target unitary.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools for understanding the fundamental limits of quantum control, which is crucial for designing quantum gates and implementing quantum algorithms using limited physical resources (i.e., only two available controls).
